info.title: Node.js HTTP status code lookup table

Index: package.json
===================================================================
--- package.json	
+++ package.json	
@@ -0,0 +1,15 @@
+{
+  "name": "http-status-server",
+  "version": "1.0.0",
+  "description": "Node.js HTTP server with an HTTP status code reason-phrase lookup table",
+  "type": "module",
+  "main": "src/server.js",

+}

+/**
+ * Look up the standard reason phrase for an HTTP status code.
+ * @param {number|string} code
+ * @returns {string|undefined} the reason phrase, or undefined if unknown
+ */
+export function getReasonPhrase(code) {
+  const key = Number(code);
+  return Object.hasOwn(STATUS_CODES, key) ? STATUS_CODES[key] : undefined;
+}

+/**
+ * Look up the class (1-5) for an HTTP status code.
+ * @param {number|string} code
+ * @returns {number|undefined} 1..5, or undefined if not a valid HTTP status code
+ */

+  const key = Number(code);
+  if (!Number.isInteger(key) || key < 100 || key > 599) return undefined;
+  return Math.trunc(key / 100);
+}
+
+export default STATUS_CODES;

/**
 * Look up the standard reason phrase for an HTTP status code.
 * @param {number|string} code
 * @returns {string|undefined} the reason phrase, or undefined if unknown
 */
export function getReasonPhrase(code) {
  const key = Number(code);
  return Object.hasOwn(STATUS_CODES, key) ? STATUS_CODES[key] : undefined;
}

/**

 * @param {number|string} code

export function getStatusCodeClass(code) {
  const key = Number(code);
  if (!Number.isInteger(key) || key < 100 || key > 599) return undefined;
  return Math.trunc(key / 100);
}

export default STATUS_CODES;

All tests pass. Let me do a quick smoke test of the server startup as well. Actually tests already cover the server. Let me verify start works briefly. Not strictly necessary. I'll do a quick one to confirm.

Let me run the server and curl it. Actually, I can just trust tests. But a quick smoke is nice confidence. Let me do it in one command with a background process. Actually keep it simple, tests cover it. 

I'll summarize. Note the task didn't ask me to commit, so I won't.

Project scaffolded and all 6 tests pass.

**Layout**
- `package.json` — ESM, Node >=18, `start`/`test` scripts, zero dependencies
- `src/status-codes.js` — frozen lookup table of ~60 standard codes plus `getReasonPhrase()` and `getStatusCodeClass()`
- `src/server.js` — HTTP server exposing `/` and `/status/:code`, exportable `createApp()` for testing
- `test/status-codes.test.js` — unit + endpoint tests using `node:test`
- `.gitignore`

Run with `npm start` (defaults to `0.0.0.0:3000`, override via `HOST`/`PORT`), e.g. `curl localhost:3000/status/404` → `{"code":404,"reason":"Not Found","class":4,"category":"4xx"}`.

One note: `getReasonPhrase(404)` returns the reason phrase, while the server returns HTTP 404 for an *unknown* lookup code — the response body still contains the requested code, so the semantics stay clear.
